metadata.title: Salmon Wallet — The Open Wallet Layer for Solana
metadata.description: Open-source, self-custodial Solana wallet — and an open distribution layer for emerging protocols. Live on extension, web, and Android.

hero.heading: Open code. No gatekeepers.
hero.subheading: Salmon is an open-source, self-custodial Solana wallet — and an open distribution layer for the protocols building there. Live on extension, web, and Android.

chains.heading: Multi-chain by design
chains.subheading: Manage assets across Solana and Bitcoin — including devnets and testnets.

why.heading: The problem is not custody. It is control.
why.subheading: Crypto users hold their keys — but closed wallets still decide what gets integrated, what gets surfaced, and who gets distribution. That is not neutral infrastructure. That is private control over a critical layer.

closed.label: The closed wallet layer
items: A private roadmap decides what gets surfaced, integrated, and prioritized.
Protocols pitch a business development team — and wait.
Defaults and integrations users cannot inspect.

open.label: The open wallet layer
items: Integrations are reviewed in public and land on merit.
You open a pull request, not a partnership deck.
Every default and integration is public code.

why.kicker: Wallets are not just UX — they are distribution infrastructure. The more important the access layer becomes, the more transparent, verifiable, and forkable it should be.

protocols.heading: Open the wallet layer.
protocols.subheading: Emerging Solana protocols should not have to wait for a private company to decide whether they deserve access to users. Salmon gives them an open path.

items.title: Built for distribution
items.description: An integration should bring users, not just another logo for a deck. Salmon is designed so protocols can turn integrations into traction, feedback, and repeat usage.

items.title: A direct path to users
items.description: Ship your integration, onboard the community that follows it, and keep a feedback loop that no closed roadmap can cut off.

items.title: Open review, not closed doors
items.description: Every integration is reviewed in public before it ships — security first. The bar is code quality, not a business deal.

features.heading: Everything you need in a Solana wallet. Nothing you can't verify.
features.subheading: One reliable path: create or import a wallet, receive funds, transact — and use the integration that brought you here.

send.title: Send & receive
send.description: Move tokens and NFTs on Solana with a wallet that stays out of your way.

swap.title: Swap in-wallet
swap.description: Trade tokens directly from the wallet — no extra sites, no custodial detour.

custody.title: Self-custodial by design
custody.description: Keys are encrypted on your device and never leave it. Custody stays with you.

validator.title: An active Solana validator
validator.description: Salmon runs its own validator — skin in the game, live and verifiable on-chain.

opensource.title: Open-source, all of it
opensource.description: The code behind every flow is public — inspect it, challenge it, fork it.

nfts.title: NFTs included
nfts.description: Store, view, and send your NFTs alongside your tokens.

dapps.title: Connect to dApps
dapps.description: You approve every connection explicitly — you decide what each app can see.

chains.title: Solana + Bitcoin
chains.description: Built for Solana first, with Bitcoin support — devnets and testnets included.

security.heading: Security is a product decision.
security.subheading: Not only code — discipline. The most important wallet actions must work reliably before anything else gets layered on top.

items.title: Keys stay with you
items.description: Your private keys are encrypted on your device and protected by your password. Salmon is built so custody stays with the user.

items.title: Privacy with restraint
items.description: Salmon is designed to minimize unnecessary data collection and reduce hidden extraction at the interface layer.

items.title: Open security model
items.description: Security improves through transparency. Open-source code, public review, continuous testing, and audit readiness create a verifiable security posture.

items.title: Visible review, accountable shipping
items.description: Critical infrastructure should not evolve behind closed doors. Changes are reviewed, challenged, and improved in the open.

manifesto.heading: Salmon is not here to blend in.
manifesto.subheading: It is here to open one of crypto's most important control layers.

principles.title: Built for protocols that need reach. Not permission.
principles.description: If protocols cannot reach users, they do not have a growth problem. They have an access problem.

principles.title: Built for users who care what they depend on.
Open-source is not branding.
principles.description: It is the point. Closed infrastructure creates invisible power.

principles.title: Traction first. Narrative second.
principles.description: If nobody uses it, nothing else matters. Credibility is earned through protocols integrating, users arriving, and communities returning.

principles.title: If Salmon wins, it wins in public.
principles.description: If it fails, it fails in public too.

items.question: What is Salmon?
items.answer: Salmon is an open-source, self-custodial wallet built as open wallet infrastructure. It helps emerging Solana protocols distribute their integrations, and helps their communities access them without depending on closed wallet-layer decisions.

items.question: Does Salmon have access to my private keys?
items.answer: No. Your private keys are encrypted locally on your device and remain under your control. If you lose your recovery phrase, no one can recover it for you.

items.question: Why would a user switch to Salmon?
items.answer: Because Salmon is not only about storing assets. It is about access. Users come to Salmon to use integrations, support emerging ecosystems, and avoid closed wallet-layer gatekeeping.

items.question: Why would a protocol integrate Salmon?
items.answer: Because distribution matters. Salmon gives protocols a way to ship integrations, onboard real users, gather feedback, and create measurable traction through an open wallet layer.

items.question: Is Salmon really open-source?
items.answer: Yes. Salmon's core software is open-source and available through its public repositories on GitHub.

items.question: Is Salmon audited?
items.answer: Salmon follows an open security model built around reviews, continuous testing, and audit readiness. Security is treated as an ongoing process, not a one-time marketing claim.

items.question: Can I use Salmon today?
items.answer: Yes. Salmon is live across browser extension, web wallet, and Android.

items.question: What chains does Salmon support?
items.answer: Salmon is built initially around Solana, with Bitcoin support, and expands carefully where demand and alignment are strongest.

items.question: Does Salmon operate beyond the wallet itself?
items.answer: Yes. Salmon also operates an active Solana validator, reinforcing its operational alignment with the ecosystem it serves.

items.question: What does community-owned mean here?
items.answer: It should mean more than feature requests or symbolic participation. The goal is to align the project's future with structures that can represent real ownership and governance over the core assets and direction of Salmon.

items.question: What would SAL represent?
items.answer: SAL should represent meaningful alignment around the future of the project, not just a token added to finance a wallet. The long-term objective is for ownership and governance to be tied to the real infrastructure, assets, and direction that make Salmon valuable.

items.question: Does Salmon collect user data?
items.answer: Salmon is designed to reduce unnecessary data collection and hidden extraction at the interface layer. For implementation details and current policy, see the Privacy Policy.

items.question: What happens if Salmon stops operating?
items.answer: Salmon is open-source infrastructure. Even if the original team disappears, the code remains accessible and the project can continue to evolve in the open rather than disappear behind a closed company structure.
